_meta.description: Deterministic clause-tag -> controlling-authority map. Statute AND case-law anchors. Every entry's `citation` is verified against a primary source via WebFetch; the audit trail (URL + method per entry) lives in CITATION_MAP_SIGNOFF.md. This map is the ONLY citation source rendered to users; the LLM proposer (agent/citation_linker.py) is graded against it and never reaches user-facing output.
_meta.lookup: lookup_citation(tag, jurisdiction_hint=None) returns the first entry whose tag matches; when jurisdiction_hint is given it is preferred. Entries are ordered so the canonical controlling authority for each tag is first. Tags with no entry (e.g. accelerated_vesting -> contract-anchored) return None by design.

entries.rationale: Delaware merger statute: board resolution plus a majority stockholder vote to adopt a merger agreement. A change-of-control clause triggers on the very transaction this section authorizes.
Sale, lease or exchange of all or substantially all assets requires majority stockholder approval — the asset-deal route to a change of control alongside the § 251 merger route.
Hart-Scott-Rodino premerger notification and waiting period: change-of-control acquisitions over the size thresholds must notify the FTC/DOJ and observe the waiting period before closing.
Clayton Act § 7: prohibits stock or asset acquisitions whose effect may be substantially to lessen competition or tend to create a monopoly — the substantive antitrust limit on a change of control.
New York analogue to DGCL § 251: the board adopts a plan of merger or consolidation for a New York constituent corporation (shareholder authorization follows under § 903).

entries.citation: In re Trados Inc. S'holder Litig., 73 A.3d 17 (Del. Ch. 2013)
entries.rationale: Directors owe duties to common stockholders; a board conflicted by preferred-holder interests in approving a merger is judged under entire fairness — the fiduciary-duty backdrop to change-of-control deals.
Terms restricting assignment of accounts, chattel paper, payment intangibles or promissory notes are ineffective — caps the reach of a contractual no-assignment clause over receivables.
Delegation of performance and assignment of rights in sale-of-goods contracts; a bare prohibition on assigning 'the contract' bars only delegation of performance, not assignment of accrued rights.
Patents are personal property assignable only by a written instrument; governs assignment of patent rights in an M&A IP transfer and PTO recordation against later purchasers.
A transfer of copyright ownership is invalid unless in a signed written instrument of conveyance — the writing requirement for assigning copyrights in a deal.
A registered trademark is assignable only with the goodwill of the business it symbolizes; a bare 'assignment in gross' is invalid — controls trademark transfers in M&A.

entries.citation: Akorn, Inc. v. Fresenius Kabi AG, 2018 WL 4719347 (Del. Ch. Oct. 1, 2018), aff'd, 198 A.3d 724 (Del. 2018)
entries.rationale: First Delaware decision finding a Material Adverse Effect that justified terminating a merger; the controlling authority for MAC/MAE clause disputes.

entries.citation: AB Stable VIII LLC v. MAPS Hotels & Resorts One LLC, 2020 WL 7024929 (Del. Ch. Nov. 30, 2020), aff'd, 268 A.3d 198 (Del. 2021)
entries.rationale: Post-Akorn MAC / ordinary-course-covenant case: a seller's reasonable but extraordinary COVID-19 response breached the ordinary-course covenant, excusing the buyer from closing.

entries.citation: Revlon, Inc. v. MacAndrews & Forbes Holdings, Inc., 506 A.2d 173 (Del. 1986)
entries.rationale: Once a sale or break-up is inevitable, directors must maximize immediate stockholder value; no-shop / lock-up deal-protection devices that foreclose higher bids draw enhanced scrutiny.
entries.primary_source: Delaware Supreme Court (verified via Penn Carey Law DE Corp Law Resource Center)

entries.rationale: Every contract restraining a lawful profession, trade or business is void in California — the broad statutory bar on employee/seller non-competes (amended eff. Jan. 1, 2024).
